text:
eli: heads up - saw a weird tail-latency spike on host parsing after the microparse tweak landed. mostly streaming gRPC paths.

maya: saw that too. spikes at the same time as KV cache evictions. looks correlated in traces.

eli: attaching the pprof dump i grabbed from a stressed replica: 
```
http://ci-artifacts/internal/flame-1749991230.svg
(pprof top shows: net::read -> parse_frame -> tokenize -> kv_lookup)
```

sanjay: hmm, tokenize -> kv_lookup ordering is odd. microparse was supposed to short-circuit tokenization for small frames. could be a fast-path invalidation touching KV tags.

zack: @sanjay can you share the exact flag we rolled? iirc it toggles the incremental splitter heuristics + async prefetch.

sanjay: flag = `runtime.ingress.microparse_enable=true` and `runtime.ingress.kv_prefetch_async=1`. rolled in canary at 09:12 UTC yesterday.

maya: workload where it spikes: lots of 2-6 token continuation streams (chat-lite). high QPS, low token-per-request. batching heuristics try to microbatch but host parse path now does extra memcpy when prefetch misses.

eli: reproduced locally with `wrk` + trace headers. when I flip off `microparse_enable` latency tail disappears.

infra-bot: deploy rollback triggered: revert/runtime.ingress.microparse_enable -> false (by eli) 

eli: reverted the flag in canary and tails returned to baseline. rolling to dedicated to confirm. still need root cause.

zack: my suspicion: the microparse shortcut bakes in assumptions about contiguous frames. when prefetch async results in kv miss, we do extra decoder-copy and then reparse, which prevents the kernel selector from choosing the slim parse kernel (it sees larger working set). kernel selection + kv cold path interaction => worse cache lines and syscall churn.

sanjay: agreed. quick experiment idea: keep microparse but disable `kv_prefetch_async` to force sync prefetch and measure. if tail goes away it's the interleaving.

maya: running that now on canary cluster-2. will post numbers in a min.

(5m later) maya: numbers: 99.9th before revert = 420ms, after revert = 95ms, microparse + sync-prefetch = 110ms. so sync-prefetch mostly recovers. async-prefetch + microparse is the combo that regresses.

eli: good signal. we should: 1) add a micro-benchmark that simulates async prefetch miss + token-split to CI; 2) update kernel selector to inspect a short-circuit hint instead of raw buffer size; 3) add metric for `parse_reparse_count`.

zack: +1 to metrics. also add a small unit in `ingress/parse` that emits a tag when async-prefetch returned miss and caused reparse so we can quickly triage in prod without pprof.

sanjay: i'll own a minimal patch that bypasses the extra memcpy on async miss (move to in-place reparse) and add `parse_reparse_count` metric. will open PR with bench results.

eli: thanks. please include microbenchmark comparing kernel selection decisions (slim vs full parse) before/after. i want to see the kernel selection state.

maya: opened canary with `kv_prefetch_async=0` and microparse on for 2h. telemetry looks stable. pushing a test to reproduce in perf lab (deterministic workernode).

zack: also we should document the gotcha in the release notes: "microparse + async-prefetch can cause reparse-induced kernel selection regression under low-token streams". short-term mitigation: disable `kv_prefetch_async` on chat-lite customers.

eli: agreed. SANDBOX TODOs: 
- @sanjay patch to avoid memcpy on async miss (PR open)
- add `parse_reparse_count` and a short metric tag
- bench + kernel-selector instrumentation in CI
- release note + ops runbook for rollback

sanjay: PR #4129 incoming, will add bench and metric.

maya: i'll follow up with a perf writeup (short) once PR lands. includes flamegraphs and the `wrk` script.

eli: cool. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
